OpenH1 logo board, round 5

Six panels for the Hull Marking direction, each a standalone icon seen straight on, with OPEN stencilled above H1 in fresh paint: the H white, the 1 military orange, on a dark grey-green hull.

Drawn flat-shaded like a technical illustration so they can be modelled: one light from the top left; raised parts have light upper-left bevels, dark lower-right bevels and a hard shadow; recesses are the other way round, with a dark top wall and a lit bottom wall. Small versions use a slightly darker plate (#353d37) so the orange 1 keeps contrast at 16 pixels. Files are in website/logo/round5/, made by website/logo/round5/build.py.

01

A door in a raised frame

Access Hatch

An access hatch: a raised frame with five bolts, the door set into it on two hinges, a recessed handle at the bottom, and OPEN over H1 painted on the door, divided by a thin rule. The literal reading: a door marked open.

Why it's safe. An original panel drawn here, with our own stencil letters. No emblem, insignia, unit name or lettering from the series.

Why it's not UNSC or Xbox. Not UNSC: no eagle, globe, wings or star, and none of its type. Not Xbox: grey-green, white and orange, no X, orb or green.

Vehicle armour plate

Side Armour

A vehicle's side armour: an asymmetric plate with its corners cut, a thick raised border carrying two offset rows of bolts, and the field recessed inside it, with OPEN in white over H1.

Crate End

The end panel of an equipment crate: bolted triangular corner guards that stand proud of the panel, a band of black and orange caution stripes, and OPEN over H1 stencilled between them, as if on the lid of the kit.

Faceted Plate

An angular plate pressed into a flat top face with deep chamfered facets all round, lit from the top left so the facets read as solid form; a bolt on each side facet, and OPEN over H1 on the top face.

Stacked Plates

Two layers: OPEN stencilled on a base plate, and below it a smaller badge plate bolted on with four bolts, standing proud and casting a hard shadow, with H1 on it. The badge's edge is the rule between the words.

Why it's safe. An original panel drawn here, with our own stencil letters. No emblem, insignia, unit name or lettering from the series.

Vent Panel

A service panel with four corner bolts and a recessed grille of four louvres cut into its lower third; OPEN over H1 above it. The vents give it a machine's purpose and a clear bottom to the composition.

At small size

Each panel's small version at its true 16 pixels in a light and a dark browser tab, on white and on dark, the one-colour mark at 16 pixels, and the small version enlarged eight times. OPEN drops out below 32 pixels; the silhouette and H1 carry the icon.

Top two

Close behind: Faceted Plate has the boldest silhouette and the simplest model; Side Armour is the most vehicle-like. Crate End is the only one carrying the caution stripes, which suit it but make it the busiest small.

No. 1

Stacked Plates

The clearest structure of the six: OPEN on the base, H1 on a plate bolted over it, so the two words get their own layers and the badge's edge does the work of the rule. It has the strongest depth story for the 3D model (a base, a plate standing proud, a hard shadow, four bolts), and it reduces cleanly at 16 pixels to H1 on a lighter plate.

No. 2

Access Hatch

The best idea: a door, marked open. It reads as a real piece of hull straight away, has the richest set of raised and recessed parts to model (frame, door, hinges, handle recess, bolts), and the thin rule between OPEN and H1 keeps the lettering calm. At 16 pixels it is an H1 on a plate with a handle slot.
